title: Seal planning authority in the shipped journey chains
description:
Make the product's shipped planning journey actually SEAL authority bodies, so downstream approved-plan readers (task-47b2dbc6, the c320c34a Foundation matrix) read real sealed content instead of the ABSENT arm.

MEASURED GAP (worker-40cfc767 probe at 6755d22, comment-66daafd0 on task-2cc6c59d): after a full bootstrapSequence() drive through the production send() pipeline, planning-authority/run-1 holds ZERO events — planning-authority-persistence.ts:120-132 authorityOf() reads member "authority" off the chain's last command, finds none (neither planningChain()/finalizeChain() at bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:216-299 nor demo-seed-payloads.ts carries one), takes the ABSENT branch at :189, and finalize's carried={} spreads nothing onto the run record.

THE CHANGE: add the authority member {acceptanceContract, planRevision} to the finalize/propose chain in bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts AND demo-seed-payloads.ts (shape precedent: planning-authority-persistence.test.ts:103-110). The LEGACY pinned contract at planning-authority-persistence.test.ts:257-266 ("legacy arm stays byte-identical", empty aggregate asserted) covers chains WITHOUT the member and MUST STAY GREEN UNTOUCHED — this row adds the member to the shipped chains, it does not flip the legacy arm.

BLAST RADIUS, pre-measured by the run-not-grep rule: 18 test files reference approval.decide/approvalPayload/bootstrapSequence/driveThrough (planning-services 62 occurrences, demo-seed-plan 8, bootstrap-durability 6, agent-wrapper 5, affordance-read 5, bootstrap-finalize-journey 5). Planner MUST apply the flip-and-run pre-measure (apply locally, run daemon suite once, read dominant reason code) — grep radius has no consistent sign (recorded: e194c5f6 under-counted, f216f085 over-counted).

SEQUENCING: NOT a prerequisite of task-2cc6c59d (its rail was amended to conditional binding, comment-5aaf5455 — forward-compatible with this row). IS the value-completer for task-47b2dbc6's readers and the c320c34a matrix. Coordinate with f216f085's landed two-request form: the finalize rides its own plan.propose envelope (PLANNING_FINALIZE_CHAIN_MIXED forbids mixing terminals in one chain) — decide explicitly which request carries the authority member and record why.

Preserve the negative worlds (standing condition): at least one seeder keeps an authority-LESS chain so the ABSENT arm and 2cc6c59d's new INCONSISTENCY refusal keep reachable homes; bootstrap-journey-fixtures.ts's proposedNotFinalizedStore() pattern is the precedent.
definitionOfDone: The shipped journey (bootstrapSequence + demo seed) seals authority: after a full production-pipeline drive, planning-authority/<runId> holds the BodiesSealed/EnvelopeSealed events and the run record carries authorityRef + envelopeDigest + bodiesDigest via the LEG branch
The legacy pinned contract (planning-authority-persistence.test.ts legacy arm, empty aggregate) stays byte-identical and green — untouched
At least one seeder retains an authority-less chain as the durable home for the ABSENT arm, with an inline comment naming its consumers (2cc6c59d inconsistency refusal, persistence ABSENT arm)
Radius absorbed by measurement not grep: the flip-and-run pre-measure recorded verbatim in the plan; every reddened suite either fixed in-scope or explicitly routed with its owner named
Gates: daemon typecheck + daemon test exit 0 with count arithmetic recorded; explicit-pathspec commit; path-attributed baseline for foreign reds

Worlds and payloads, never assertions weakened: consumer suites' expectation churn is absorbed by updating expected values to the measured new reality, not by deleting arms; the acc1a3b4/f216f085 negative-worlds discipline applies

implementationPlan.description: RAIL 2 IS ALREADY ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT — VERIFY IT, THEN STOP LOOKING. Rail 2 says the authority member rides the request the persistence layer reads it from, and to measure which rather than assume. I measured it; re-confirm these four reads at your HEAD before touching anything, because getting this wrong produces an edit that looks correct in a diff and does NOTHING. (1) `planning-services.ts:132` — `if (terminal.kind === "FINALIZE") return commitFinalizedSubmission(context, runId, prior, folded);` RETURNS EARLY, before `buildPlanningAuthorityLeg` is called at `:136`. **The FINALIZE request therefore never reads an authority member at all.** (2) `:136-138` passes `lastCommand: commands[commands.length - 1]` — the last command of the chain being folded. (3) `planning-authority-persistence.ts:120-132 authorityOf()` reads member "authority" off exactly that command and returns `undefined` when absent, which becomes `{kind:"ABSENT"}` at `:189`. (4) `:141 const carried = authority.kind === "LEG" ? authority.binding : {}`. CONCLUSION, and it is the load-bearing decision of this row: **the authority member goes on the LAST COMMAND OF `planningChain()` — the PROPOSE request — never on `finalizeChain()`.** f216f085 landed the two-request form: `bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:216 planningChain()` still ends at plan.propose (which is exactly why the legacy pin survives), and `:276 finalizeChain()` rides its own envelope at `:423` with commandId `cmd-finalize`. Putting the member on the finalize chain honours PLANNING_FINALIZE_CHAIN_MIXED, reads plausibly, and is INERT. Record this conclusion with the four line references in a task comment before editing. THEN THE FLIP-AND-RUN PRE-MEASURE, which rail/DoD 4 make binding and which a grep cannot answer: apply the member to both builders locally, run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` ONCE, and read the DOMINANT REASON CODE off the failures. Grep radius has no consistent sign on this board — e194c5f6 UNDER-counted (17 by grep, ~26 real), f216f085 OVER-counted (10 named, fewer real). Write your churn set from the run. implementationPlan.note:
HARNESS CHAIN SEALS — with ONE deviation from the step text, taken on measurement and recorded rather than done silently.

DEVIATION: the member is NOT put inside `planningChain()`. It is overlaid at the CALL SITE by a new `sealedPlanningChain()`, which `bootstrapSequence()` uses; `planningChain()` stays BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD and authority-less. This is step 6's second option, and step 1's flip-and-run proved it is the one that is true at this HEAD: sealing the shared builder reddened the legacy pin's two arms (persistence.test.ts:262 readEvents toEqual([]), :273 keys not toContain "authority") AND four planning-services.test.ts arms whose subject is the human-authority gate, which would have been a refusal answered at the wrong layer. Sealing at the call site leaves all of them green for the RIGHT reason and hands DoD 3 its authority-less home for free: `planningChain()` itself.

THE COUPLING IS REPRODUCED, both halves:
- `submissionHash` on the same command, set to the minted plan's own `planHash` (SEALED_SUBMISSION_HASH), because buildPlanningAuthorityLeg reads submissionHash off folded state and refuses PLANNING_AUTHORITY_STATE_UNSEALED / PLANNING_AUTHORITY_SUBMISSION_HASH_MISMATCH otherwise. It is DERIVED, never spelled — a constant and a minted body cannot be kept in agreement by hand.
- EXACTLY TWO KEYS on the member (acceptanceContract, planRevision). authorityOf's `Reflect.ownKeys(member).length !== AUTHORITY_KEYS.length` is a hard PLANNING_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED, so the interface documents the arity where a future editor will see it.
- Bodies minted through @moe/core's OWN createPlanRevision/createAcceptanceContract, never hand-authored bytes; both refusals are thrown with code@layer rather than swallowed.

Two knock-on values had to follow the sealed hash or the journey refuses BOOTSTRAP_REVISION_HASH_MISMATCH: finalizeChain()'s revision.planHash, and approvalPayload()'s default record hash. The LEGACY constant survives as an export (`SUBMISSION_HASH = hex64("dec0de")`) and is still what the authority-less world uses.
